info.name: Bills Backend
info.description:
Test calls for the Mi MDev bills backend.

WHERE THE CALLS GO. baseUrl is the production server (https://api.dizztech.com). To work against your own computer pick the "Mi MDev - Local" environment (baseUrl http://localhost:8080, started with `go run .`); "Mi MDev - Production" is the same as the default. CAUTION: with production selected, "Orders (app API)" really creates orders and the simulated webhooks are real requests.

TWO KINDS OF "DIRECT" FOLDERS. "ABS Vendor (direct)", "Email (direct)", "Monnify (direct)" and "Kora (direct)" call the TEST ROUTES OF OUR OWN SERVER (/abs, /monnify, /kora, /email), to test the backend's own provider clients with the keys in the server's settings. The server serves them only while APP_ENV=sandbox AND ABS_SANDBOX=true (otherwise 404, as on production and on a server running with live ABS settings), and they need the admin token when ADMIN_TOKEN is set. "ABS (direct to ABS)", "Kora (direct to Kora)", "Monnify collections (direct to Monnify)", "Monnify Bills (direct to Monnify)" and "ZeptoMail (direct)" call the PROVIDERS themselves with your own keys, which you put in the variables' CURRENT values (they stay on your computer; do not type keys into the initial values, which are saved in this file). Use them to check a provider on its own, whatever build is running.

The /admin requests are always served and always need the token in production. The app does not use ABS vouchers; /abs/voucher is only for testing ABS itself. Every response from our server uses one envelope: {"status":"successful"|"failed","message":"...","data":{...},"error":"..."}. Look under `data` for the payload; `error` is only present when status is "failed".

item.name: ABS Vendor (direct)

request.description: ABS's live catalog: airtime providers, data plans, electricity services, voucher providers. Use it to find the ids the calls below need.
network is an AIRTIME product trackid. Minimum 50 naira. The reply has sandbox:true unless ABS_SANDBOX=false.
network is a DATA network trackid (different from the airtime id) and plan is a plan trackid.
Minimum 1000 naira. Run Validate meter first.
quantity is 1-30.
Looks up an order ABS already accepted. Set absOrderId to the id ABS gave the order (the order_id in ABS webhooks).

item.description: Calls ABS's Direct API through the backend. Purchases are only validated while ABS_SANDBOX=true.

request.description: Sends one email through ZeptoMail directly, bypassing the order flow. With MAIL_SANDBOX=true (the default) nothing is sent, the reply says so; set MAIL_SANDBOX=false to actually deliver.
Optional: name, description, reference, expires_in_minutes (default 30).
Uses the reference saved by Create invoice.
Asks Monnify about the payment itself: payment_status (PAID, PARTIALLY_PAID, OVERPAID, PENDING...) and amount_paid_naira vs total_payable_naira. Use the transaction_reference from Create invoice.

Needs PAYMENT_PROVIDER=kora and a Kora test secret key. Asks Kora for a one-time bank account. Optional: name, reference (at least 8 characters). In test mode Kora pays it for you after about 2 minutes. This is also the first call to run: it settles the endpoint path, which Kora's text guide does not print.
Kora's Transaction Query. status is PAID, PENDING or FAILED; amount_accepted_naira is the amount we may give value for (Kora's amount_accepted).

item.name: Monnify Bills (direct to Monnify)
item.description: Walks Monnify Bills Payment step by step, calling Monnify itself rather than this backend, to learn how the API behaves before anything is built. Run 1 to 4 to browse, 5 to validate, 6 to vend, 7 to requery.

request.description: Calls Monnify directly (not this backend). Fill monnifyApiKey and monnifySecretKey in the collection variables; monnifyBaseUrl defaults to the sandbox. Saves the access token for the other requests. Never commit or share a collection with real keys filled in.
Read only. AIRTIME, DATA_BUNDLE, DATA, ELECTRICITY, CABLE_TV, BETTING, EDUCATION and TRANSPORTATION were returned for the first account tested.
Read only. Set categoryCode first (for example ELECTRICITY, AIRTIME, DATA_BUNDLE or DATA). Saves the first biller code as billerCode; change it to pick another.

Read only. This is where a product's price, any fee and any commission would show; look at every field of the reply. Saves the first product as productCode (field name is read as code, or productCode).
Read only. Checks a meter, phone or smart card number. If vendInstruction.requireValidationRef is true the vend needs the validationReference, which this request saves.

SANDBOX ONLY unless you mean it: on a live account this debits your Monnify wallet. A fresh unique reference is generated for each send and saved as billsReference. validationReference is sent only if the validate step produced one. Set billAmount and customerId first.
Read only. Status is IN_PROGRESS, SUCCESS or FAILED. Run it after Vend, or any time the vend reply was unclear.

item.name: Orders (app API)

request.description:
Amounts here are in kobo. Send the same idempotency_key twice to see the same order come back.

`customer_name` is optional and defaults to the email's local part; it is stored on the order and used both for the Monnify invoice and for the purchase-successful receipt email (if ZeptoMail is configured).

The reply has amount_kobo (what is bought), fee_kobo (the electricity service fee, 0 otherwise) and total_kobo (what the customer pays, and what the account number waits for).

note (when present) is the plan's own warning from ABS, kept on the order as it was when the customer ordered, for example a fair use limit or "wont credit if user has an outstanding debt". Show it before the customer pays.

The price comes from the catalog, so no amount is sent. plan_id is a data plan id from GET /v1/catalog.

The reply has amount_kobo (what is bought), fee_kobo (the electricity service fee, 0 otherwise) and total_kobo (what the customer pays, and what the account number waits for).

note (when present) is the plan's own warning from ABS, kept on the order as it was when the customer ordered, for example a fair use limit or "wont credit if user has an outstanding debt". Show it before the customer pays.

FibreX plans (recipient_type "fn", category "FibreX" in the catalog) are bought for a FibreX FN: two letters FN and 6 digits. ABS's "ODU" plans look similar in the catalog but are bought for an ordinary phone number (recipient_type "phone"); use the same Create order (data) request for those.

The reply has amount_kobo (what is bought), fee_kobo (the electricity service fee, 0 otherwise) and total_kobo (what the customer pays, and what the account number waits for).

note (when present) is the plan's own warning from ABS, kept on the order as it was when the customer ordered, for example a fair use limit or "wont credit if user has an outstanding debt". Show it before the customer pays.

Call "Validate meter" first and show the owner to the customer; the backend does not check the meter itself at order time. Minimum 1000 naira (100000 kobo). The token appears as `delivery` on the order once it succeeds.

`customer_name` is optional and defaults to the email's local part; it is stored on the order and used both for the Monnify invoice and for the purchase-successful receipt email (if ZeptoMail is configured).

The reply has amount_kobo (what is bought), fee_kobo (the electricity service fee, 0 otherwise) and total_kobo (what the customer pays, and what the account number waits for).

note (when present) is the plan's own warning from ABS, kept on the order as it was when the customer ordered, for example a fair use limit or "wont credit if user has an outstanding debt". Show it before the customer pays.
Free. Shows who the meter belongs to so the customer can confirm before paying.

Uses the id saved by Create order (ids look like MDEV_ followed by 16 letters and digits, for example MDEV_7K3QX9M2PA4B8WDH; orders made before 19 Oct 2026 have 32 hex characters).

While the order is AWAITING_PAYMENT or PARTIALLY_PAID, each call (at most once every 5 seconds per order) also asks Monnify whether it was paid, so the order moves on even if the webhook never arrives. When an order reaches SUCCESS and ZeptoMail is configured, the customer is emailed a receipt (to test it: pay the order in Monnify's bank simulator and set MAIL_SANDBOX=false, using your own email on the order).

Prices here are what customers pay: ABS's price marked up per network (MTN 2.5%, 2.2% from ₦20,000; Airtel 4%; Glo 5%), rounded up to ₦5. Plans ABS runs as promotions (names with HOT DEAL, CHEAP OFFER or BEST DEAL) are in their own "Deals" category, first in each network. A few plans are hidden on purpose. The reply also has electricity_fee {min_kobo, percent}: the service fee on electricity is the greater of the two, rounded up to whole naira, so the app can show the total before ordering. The vendor cost is never in this reply.

Operator view of every order, newest first. Optional status (comma separated) and limit (1-200, default 50). Statuses: INITIATED, AWAITING_PAYMENT, PAID, PARTIALLY_PAID, OVERPAID, VENDING, SUCCESS, PENDING, FAILED, REFUND_DUE, REFUNDED, EXPIRED, CANCELLED. Each order includes network_name and plan_name (the catalog's display names as they were when the order was placed; blank on orders from before they were stored). Needs the admin token.
Every webhook exactly as received, newest first. Optional provider (monnify or abs) and limit (1-200, default 20). Needs the admin token.

The business at a glance for a window of Nigerian days (inclusive; without from and to it is the last 30 days). Money is in kobo. orders: counts by status and the failure rate. money: revenue, service fees, vendor cost, payment fees, profit, margin, average order, the payment fees paid on orders that were never delivered, and net profit. Profit counts only delivered orders whose cost was kept (orders_without_cost says how many older ones are left out). at_risk: money held in REFUND_DUE, PENDING, VENDING and wrong-amount orders. Also by_kind, by_network, top_plans and a daily series that includes empty days. Needs the admin token.

What ABS and the payment provider are holding, in kobo. ABS comes from the account profile (only the wallet is read). The Kora balance call has not been tried against Kora yet; if it fails the error is shown and the ABS balance still appears. Needs the admin token.

Closes an order that is in REFUND_DUE after you have sent the money back by hand (this moves no money itself), so the app stops saying it is waiting for a refund. Every field is optional: refund_fee_kobo is what sending the refund cost (it reduces the net profit in /admin/stats), note is for the record, payment_fee_returned: true says the payment provider gave back its fee on the original payment. 409 for an order that is not in REFUND_DUE, 404 for an unknown one. Needs the admin token. refund_amount_kobo is what you actually sent back to the customer: leave it out for the whole total, or give the smaller amount when you deducted the costs of the transaction (it is shown to the customer as refunded_kobo and the difference counts as money kept in /admin/stats).

Records money the business spent that no order records, so /admin/stats can show profit_after_expenses_kobo. Only category, label and amount_kobo are required; day defaults to today (Nigerian time). Categories are free text; hosting, email, agent_fee, domain and transfer_duty are the ones in use (the 50 naira duty on our own transfers of 10,000 naira or more, such as ABS top-ups, belongs under transfer_duty). Needs the admin token.
Expenses for a window of Nigerian days (default the last 30), newest first, with the total and the total per category.
Removes a wrongly entered expense by its id (shown when it was added or listed). 404 if there is no such expense.

Every setting that can be changed without a restart: its current value, its .env default, source ("api" if it was changed here, "default" otherwise) and whether this server can use it (the alerts and mail ones need the email settings in .env). Never settable here: keys and secrets, the admin token, the payment provider, ABS_SANDBOX, APP_ENV, the database path and the port. Needs the admin token.

Changes one setting; it applies from the next order or catalog fetch (orders already made keep their price) and survives a restart. The value may be a number, a string, a boolean or, for hidden_plans, a list of strings. The same rules as startup apply: every markup at least 2%, the electricity fee at least 1.7%; a refused change changes nothing (400). 404 for an unknown key, 409 for a setting that needs the email settings when they are not configured. Setting mail.sandbox to false makes receipts and alerts really send.
Removes the change, so the setting follows .env again.
The latest changes to settings, newest first, with what each was before and after. Optional limit (1 to 200, default 50).

item.description: The real purchase flow: create an order, pay into the account it returns, then poll the order.

request.description: Sandbox only: signatures are not checked outside production. Set transactionReference to the one returned by Create order. The backend still asks Monnify whether the invoice is really PAID, so an unpaid invoice will not vend.

Kora webhooks are always signature checked. The pre-request script signs the data object with the koraSecretKey variable (HMAC SHA256, hex) and sets x-korapay-signature. Set orderId to the id from Create order. The backend still asks Kora what was really paid, so an unpaid order will not vend.
Only works unsigned when ABS_WEBHOOK_SECRET is empty. Events are just logged for now.

Which build is running and in what mode, for any admin token (viewers too). version is the release it was built as, like 1.0.0, taken from the git tag (1.0.0-3-g1a2b3c4 means 3 commits after that release, and "-uncommitted" means the folder had changes when it was built), go_version, env (production or sandbox), abs_sandbox (ABS only validates, never charges), direct_test_routes (true only while the /abs, /kora, /monnify and /email test routes are served: sandbox with ABS_SANDBOX=true), payment_provider, started_at (unix seconds) and uptime_seconds. Use it to check a deploy is live, and to see which mode a local server is in when a test route gives 404.
The name and role of the token being used: "owner" for ADMIN_TOKEN, otherwise the name the token was given, with its role (admin or viewer). A dashboard can call this after sign in.

Every named token, working ones first: id, name, role, the last 4 characters (hint), who made it, when it was last used and from where, and when it was revoked (0 while it works). Never the token itself. Owner only (403 for any other token).

Makes a named token, one per person or device. role is "admin" (reads and changes everything except tokens) or "viewer" (reads only; every change is refused with 403, and it cannot read the audit log). The token is in the answer ONCE and is stored only as a hash, so copy it now. The test script saves it as the variable newAdminToken. Names: 1 to 40 letters, digits, spaces, dots, dashes, underscores; "owner" and "open" are reserved; a working token with the same name gives 409. The owner is emailed when a token is made.
Stops a token working at once and for good (the row stays so the audit log can still name it). 404 if the id does not exist or is already revoked. The owner is emailed.

item.name: Who am I, with the new token

request.description: Tries the token saved by "Make a token".

What admins changed, newest first: who (token name), their role, the address, the route (for example POST /admin/orders/{id}/refunded), the real path, the status, and the request body with anything secret removed. Reads are not logged; every change is, including a viewer being refused and an address being locked out for guessing the token. Optional: actor=<token name>, before_id=<id of the last entry you have> to page back, limit 1 to 200. Owner and admin tokens only.

What happened, newest first: orders created, paid, delivered, failed, expired and refunded (kinds order.created, order.paid, order.delivered, order.failed, order.pending, order.expired, payment.late, payment.wrong_amount, payment.unknown, refund.sent), the server starting and stopping (server.started shows the version deployed), and the server's warnings and errors (kind system). Customers' phone numbers, emails, meter numbers and tokens are removed. Filters: level = the lowest to show (info for everything, warn for warnings and errors, error), kind = an exact kind or a family ending in a dot such as order., order = an order id, since = a day (2026-10-28) or an RFC 3339 time, before_id to page back, limit 1 to 200. Each event has id, at, level, kind, order_id, message and detail (small figures such as amounts). Owner and admin tokens only.
Everything that happened to one order, newest first.
Counts of info, warning and error events in the last hours (1 to 720, default 24) and the latest error: for a badge such as "2 errors today" that opens the list. Owner and admin tokens only.

No login. The app asks this when it opens (and may ask again now and then). The three headers say who is asking: X-App (which app: mi-mdev for the customer app, dashboard for the admin app), X-Platform (android, ios, web) and X-App-Version (1.4.2). The apps should send them on EVERY request. They are self reported, so they choose which notices to show, never who may do what. Query parameters app, platform and version work too, and headers win. An unnamed caller sees only notices for everyone; an unknown version counts as the oldest.

The answer is notifications (most urgent first, at most 20) and server_time (unix seconds). Each notice has kind (info, warning, maintenance), title, body, optional link_url and link_label, starts_at, ends_at (0 = until ended), dismissible, blocking and blocking_now, block_from, block_until, and updated_at. Remember dismissals by id AND updated_at: an edited notice should show again. While blocking_now is true, new orders are being refused: show the maintenance screen and do not let the customer start a payment.
The same call as a customer app with version 1.0.0. Use it to check that a notice with max_version reaches old apps.

Every notice with who it is for, who made it and where it is in its life (status: upcoming, active or ended), newest first. Any admin token, viewers too. Filter with status=active|upcoming|ended; limit 1 to 200 (default 50).

Owner and admin tokens. A plain notice for everyone, shown from now until it is ended. kind is info, warning or maintenance. title up to 80 characters, body up to 1000. lang is optional and must be "en" for now. Times (starts_at, ends_at, block_from, block_until) can be unix seconds, an RFC 3339 time like 2026-11-03T01:00:00+01:00, or a day like 2026-11-03 (midnight Nigerian time). Leave them out for "now" and "until I end it". The answer carries the id, saved as the variable noticeId.

body.raw:
{
  "kind": "info",
  "title": "New: pay electricity bills",
  "body": "You can now buy electricity tokens in the app.",
  "link_url": "https://dizztech.com/whats-new",
  "link_label": "See what is new"
}

request.description: A scheduled maintenance. Shown to the customer app from starts_at, so people get a warning. New orders are refused (503, code maintenance) only between block_from and block_until; leave block_from out to refuse from the start and block_until out to refuse until the notice ends. Orders already paid are always completed, a retry of an order that already exists still works, and looking at an order is never refused. A notice that blocks cannot be dismissed. Ending the notice (Delete) lifts the block at once.

body.raw:
{
  "kind": "maintenance",
  "title": "Upgrade tonight",
  "body": "Orders pause from 1am to 3am while we upgrade. Anything you have already paid for will still arrive.",
  "blocking": true,
  "apps": [
    "mi-mdev"
  ],
  "starts_at": "2026-11-03T20:00:00+01:00",
  "ends_at": "2026-11-04T03:30:00+01:00",
  "block_from": "2026-11-04T01:00:00+01:00",
  "block_until": "2026-11-04T03:00:00+01:00"
}

request.description: Tells old Android apps to update, and stops them ordering. max_version is inclusive, so 1.3.9 reaches 1.3.9 and everything older, including apps that do not send a version. min_version works the same from the other side. apps and platforms are lists (leave out for everyone).

body.raw:
{
  "kind": "warning",
  "title": "Please update the app",
  "body": "This version is no longer supported. Update to keep buying.",
  "link_url": "https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.example.mimdev",
  "link_label": "Update",
  "blocking": true,
  "apps": [
    "mi-mdev"
  ],
  "platforms": [
    "android"
  ],
  "max_version": "1.3.9"
}

request.description: Replaces the notice with what is sent (send the whole notice, as when making one). Not possible once it has ended: 409, make a new one. Changing it bumps updated_at, so apps show it again to people who dismissed the old text.
Ends it at this moment: it disappears from the app and, if it was stopping orders, orders flow again. It stays in the admin list as ended (an audit trail). Ending twice gives 409.

item.name: ABS (direct to ABS)
item.description: These direct folders talk to the provider itself, with your own key, so they work against any build (even production, where the /abs, /kora, /monnify and /email test routes of our own server are switched off). Put the key in the variable's CURRENT value (it stays on your computer); never type it in the initial value, which is saved in this file. Spend requests below send sandbox=1, so ABS only validates and does not charge or deliver; remove that row to make a REAL purchase.

request.description: ABS's catalog: networks, data plans, electricity services with the ids used below. About 600 KB. ABS allows 300 requests an hour per key, so do not hammer it.

The wallet is data.user_wallets[0].walletbal. WARNING: the reply also holds personal details (name, phone, email, bank accounts); do not share a screenshot or paste it anywhere. This endpoint is not in ABS's documentation, so it could change.
Read only: returns the meter owner's name and address. provider_tid is an electricity service trackid from the catalog.
airtimetid is the network id from the catalog. amount is whole naira, minimum 50. sandbox=1 = validate only. Remove the sandbox row for a REAL purchase that spends your wallet.
airtimetid is the network id and cardunittid the plan id (the bouquet trackid) from the catalog. sandbox=1 = validate only. Remove it for a REAL purchase.

provider_tid is the electricity service from the catalog, amount is whole naira (minimum 1000). Some services add a fee of their own (ABS took 1100 for a 1000 purchase on one): the backend leaves those out of the app. sandbox=1 = validate only.

Looks an order up by the ABS order id (ident) that live airtime and data replies carry in data.ident. Answers successful, Processing, failed or Refund. Partner endpoints only accept calls from an address on the ABS whitelist and need a website saved under API settings (see deploy/README.md section 3); otherwise ABS says why in message.
Wallet balance and the daily cap and amount spent. Same whitelist and website requirement as the order lookup.

item.name: Kora (direct to Kora)
item.description: These direct folders talk to the provider itself, with your own key, so they work against any build (even production, where the /abs, /kora, /monnify and /email test routes of our own server are switched off). Put the key in the variable's CURRENT value (it stays on your computer); never type it in the initial value, which is saved in this file. With a LIVE key "Create a charge" opens a real one-time account (no money moves unless someone pays into it).

request.description: Opens a one-time bank account for the reference and amount (whole naira here, as Kora wants it). merchant_bears_cost true means the customer pays exactly this amount and Kora's fee comes out of what we settle. The test script saves the reference as koraReference.
The charge's status, amount_paid, amount_accepted (what counts) and fee. This is what the backend asks Kora after every payment webhook; it never trusts the webhook's own amount.

What Kora holds for you. The backend reads the NGN available balance from this reply for /admin/balances, and it works with the live key (the dashboard shows it). Run it here to see Kora's raw answer.

item.name: Monnify collections (direct to Monnify)
item.description: These direct folders talk to the provider itself, with your own key, so they work against any build (even production, where the /abs, /kora, /monnify and /email test routes of our own server are switched off). Put the key in the variable's CURRENT value (it stays on your computer); never type it in the initial value, which is saved in this file. (Monnify is the backup payment provider; Kora is the one in use.) Run Login first: its test script saves the access token as monnifyToken for the other requests.

request.description: Basic auth with your API key and secret key. The test script saves responseBody.accessToken as monnifyToken (valid about an hour).
Opens a one-time account for the invoice reference. expiryDate is Nigerian time, yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss. The test script saves the references as invoiceReference and transactionReference.
The invoice's status (PENDING, PAID, EXPIRED) and the account it asked the customer to pay.
What Monnify says was really paid: paymentStatus, amountPaid and totalPayable. The backend checks this after every payment webhook.

item.name: ZeptoMail (direct)
item.description: These direct folders talk to the provider itself, with your own key, so they work against any build (even production, where the /abs, /kora, /monnify and /email test routes of our own server are switched off). Put the key in the variable's CURRENT value (it stays on your computer); never type it in the initial value, which is saved in this file. This sends a REAL email to testEmail when the sender domain is verified.

request.description: Sends one message the way the backend sends receipts and alerts. The Authorization header is "Zoho-enczapikey " followed by your send mail token. mailFromEmail must belong to a domain verified in ZeptoMail. zeptoBaseUrl must match the region of your ZeptoMail account (the backend's default is https://cpaas.zoho.com).
